title: Malformed input returns 500 errors instead of 400/404
steps: GET each authenticated route ending in an ID with 'not-a-uuid' (22 routes).
expected: Invalid IDs → 404 (or 400); unsupported content type → 400/415. 500 is reserved for real server faults.
actual: 14 of 22 ID routes answer 500 for a malformed ID (Postgres rejects the cast). Login with a text/plain body answers 500. Malformed JSON correctly gives 400 and oversized bodies 413. No stack traces or SQL leak.
impact: Server-error counts, Sentry and the Telegram error alert can be inflated by anyone with junk URLs (alert fatigue, possible paging noise); clients get misleading statuses.
fix: Add one router-level param validator (the existing onlyUuid helper in routes/messages.ts) for every :id/…Id param, and guard req.body being undefined before destructuring. Add the malformed-ID probe as a Jest test over the endpoint inventory.
